svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: What each layer can catch, and why the misses happen
svg.desc: A grid. Four things that can leak out of a repository are set against the four layers that might stop them: the pre-commit hook and the pre-push hook, which publishable installs for you; GitHub push protection; and publishable check, the command you run yourself. Two rows above the grid describe the layers rather than the leaks. The first asks whether each runs without you: the hooks fire on every commit or every push, push protection on every push, and publishable check only when you remember. The second records how each is skipped: the two hooks with the no-verify flag, push protection by dismissing it, and publishable check by simply not running it. In the grid below, a green dot means the layer stops it and a red ring means it gets through, with the reason written underneath. An AWS or Stripe key is stopped by all four. A home path or a private host gets past push protection, because push protection knows key formats only. An agent's working note gets past both hooks, which have no check for it, and past push protection for the same key-formats reason. The same path already sitting in an older commit gets past both hooks because it is too far back for them, and past push protection again. publishable check is the only column that stops all four. A note records that on a first push pre-push is handed the whole history, and that a repository you are about to publish is long past that. The closing argument: every column here, publishable check included, only finds what someone wrote a pattern for. It just ships a check for those file names that the hooks do not, and reads further back. Nothing here catches a fact nobody described.
svg.text: publishable is a command-line tool that checks a git repository for things you would not want public.
Green dot: the layer stops it. Red ring: it gets through, reason underneath.
